```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(framework)
scaffold()
```

In this module you pull visit data from the study database, summarize systolic
pressure by arm and visit, and save a small dataset to `data/` for the
assignment.

## Get the data

`db_query()` runs SQL against the `study` connection in `settings.yml` and
closes the connection for you.

```{r}
visits <- db_query(
  "SELECT v.participant_id, v.visit_number, v.systolic_bp, v.weight_kg, p.treatment
   FROM visits v JOIN participants p ON p.participant_id = v.participant_id",
  "study"
)
nrow(visits)
```

## Summarize

Mean systolic pressure by arm and visit. Note the missing readings:
`na.rm = TRUE` drops them, and `n_measured` shows how many were left.

```{r}
sbp_summary <- visits |>
  group_by(treatment, visit_number) |>
  summarise(
    n_measured = sum(!is.na(systolic_bp)),
    mean_systolic = round(mean(systolic_bp, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
sbp_summary
```

## Plot

```{r}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4
ggplot(sbp_summary, aes(visit_number, mean_systolic, colour = treatment)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Visit", y = "Mean systolic pressure (mmHg)", colour = NULL)
```

The arms start close together. By visit 4 the intervention arm is about 12
mmHg lower.

## Save for the assignment

`data_save()` with dot notation writes to the course's `data/` folder and
registers the file, so the assignment can read it by name.

```{r}
data_save(visits, "data.visits_with_arm")
```

```{r}
data_list()
```

## Try it yourself

1. Change the summary to use the median. Does the picture change?
2. Add a column for the share of readings at or above 140 mmHg.
